sections.body: Ansor uses measured tensor programs, a learned cost model, and task scheduling to guide search toward high-throughput programs and subgraphs that matter for end-to-end DNN latency.
sections.heading: Tensor-program evidence in Ansor

sections.body: This concept generalizes across compiler work: machine-learning-based compilation learns from empirical program features, profile-guided classic optimization uses execution counts to focus transformations on hot paths, and Aestimo evaluates how training inputs alter feedback-directed decisions and performance.
sections.heading: Evidence across compiler optimization systems

sections.body: A useful synthesis would compare what each system treats as optimization evidence: tensor-program measurements, supervised feature labels, weighted flow-graph counts, and feedback-directed optimization logs.
sections.heading: Comparison focus

title: Empirical Models Guide Compiler Optimization Decisions
